title: Word Pattern Bijection
summary: Return whether pattern characters and whitespace-separated words form a one-to-one correspondence.
statement: Split the text on whitespace. The number of words must equal the number of pattern characters, and the correspondence must work in both directions: one character cannot represent two words and two characters cannot represent the same word.
constraints: The text contains whitespace-separated nonempty words.
Pattern and text may be empty; their token counts must still match.
hints: A valid pattern requires mappings in both directions, not just character-to-word consistency.
Split the text, reject unequal lengths, and maintain synchronized character-to-word and word-to-character maps.
Pseudocode checkpoint: identify the state, update it once per step, and return only after the word_pattern_bijection invariant is complete.
Editorial: Split the text, reject unequal lengths, and maintain synchronized character-to-word and word-to-character maps. The intended bounds are O(n) time and O(k) space.
